11	The compiler at `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/` has three stages. Each fails
12	differently and the symptoms look alike, so identify the stage before fixing.
13	
14	**Stage 1 — `hooks/session-end.py`.** Writes `scripts/session-flush-<uuid>-<YYYYMMDD>-<HHMMSS>.md`,
15	then spawns `flush.py`. Logs every firing to `scripts/flush.log` as `SessionEnd fired`.
16	If `flush.log` has no such line for days but the hook works when run by hand, sessions
17	are being *closed* rather than exited cleanly — not a config break. Self-verifying: end
18	one session normally and re-check the tail.
19	
20	**Stage 2 — `scripts/flush.py`.** Calls the Agent SDK, appends to `daily/<date>.md`, writes
21	`scripts/last-flush.json` **only on success**, and **deletes its context file on success**.
22	Therefore **every leftover `session-flush-*.md` is a flush that died**, and its datestamp
23	maps to a missing `daily/<date>.md`. That is the cheapest diagnostic in the whole system —
24	count the leftovers. A stale `last-flush.json` means flushes are *dying*, not that the hook
25	never fired. Recover one by hand:
26	`uv run --directory ~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler python scripts/flush.py <context-file> <session-id> [YYYY-MM-DD]`
27	Success = `Result: FLUSH_OK` + `Flush complete` in `flush.log`.
28	
29	**The third arg is a backfill date, added 2026-08-29.** Without it `flush.py` always writes
30	to *today's* log, so recovering old stranded files silently misfiles them under the current
31	date. Always pass the date parsed from the filename when backfilling; entries are then
32	marked `(backfilled …)`.
33	
34	**Batch-recovery trap — the 60-second dedup guard destroys data.** `flush.py` skips a run
35	whose `session_id` matches `last-flush.json` within 60s, and **deletes the context file on
36	that skip path too**. One session can have several stranded files (different timestamps), so
37	a loop that hits the same uuid twice inside a minute silently loses the second one — it still
38	prints as consumed. Hit 2026-08-29: 12 files ran, 10 flushed, 2 dropped. Before trusting a
39	batch, check `grep -c "Skipping duplicate flush" flush.log`, and either group runs so repeats
40	of a uuid are >60s apart or run repeats individually.
41	Recovery is possible because `~/.claude` is captured to the SSD: the deleted files came back
42	from `/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/claude/claude-memory-compiler/scripts/`.
43	
44	**Stage 3 — memsearch index.** `INDEX full set: Indexed 0 chunks` in the nightly log is
45	**usually not an indexer fault** — it means nothing new arrived. A dead stage 2 starves it
46	and looks identical. Check leftovers/`last-flush.json` before suspecting memsearch.
47	memsearch is a **uv tool**: binary `~/.local/bin/memsearch`, env
48	`~/.local/share/uv/tools/memsearch/`. Test an import directly with that env's python
49	(`.../memsearch/bin/python -c "import onnxruntime"`) rather than inferring from index counts.
50	Reinstall with `uv tool install --force memsearch`, never pip — and re-apply the local flush
51	patch afterwards, which any reinstall strips.
52	
53	**`hooks/session-start.py` — rewritten 2026-08-29.** It used to paste all of
54	`knowledge/index.md` into every session. That file is ~48k chars against a 20k cap, so the
55	index was truncated mid-table **and the `## Recent Daily Log` section was pushed off the end
56	entirely** — the one part that is always relevant never arrived. It now emits a pointer
57	(article counts + paths + the `memsearch search` command) and always includes the log:
58	20,039 → 682 chars. If a session needs the index, read
59	`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/knowledge/index.md` on demand. Backups of the pre-change
60	files are `*.bak-2026-08-29` beside each.

39	and a union on that key had **zero conflicts** across 216 Mac + 348 Windows rows
40	→ 540. Same key never carried different values. See [[github-consolidation]].

43

45	COMMANDS.md asserted the 08-24 and 08-31 weeks were "gone for good". They were not — Baylor's

47	is lost only if a game was actually played inside the gap.** Verify before declaring a loss:

62

64	a missed week is permanently missing from the series, not a chore that rolls
65	forward. This is why the reminder escalates rather than silently re-queuing.

68

70	enforced on this machine rather than depending on memory. It detects captures from the

---
name: cfb-forecast-capture
description: "CFB Victory Model weekly forecast freeze — all 16 Big 12 teams via scripts/weekly_run.sh, archive mirror, Monday-anchored nag 2026-08-24 to 2027-01-23, no backfill, and how to tell a real missed week from a stale snapshot"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 330c1f71-242a-47c7-ac7b-129bd6f5dd3c
  modified: 2026-09-02T19:20:41.051Z
---

The CFB Victory Model's pre-game forecasts are frozen once per week by the
`/forecast-capture` skill, which snapshots predictions **before kickoff** and reports what
moved since the prior week.

## Scope and entry point (changed 2026-09-02, per Eric)

- **All 16 Big 12 teams every week**, not Baylor only. The list is the `BIG12` constant in
  `weekly_capture.py` — one home; do not copy team lists into the wrapper or the skill.
  `--teams`/`--team` still narrow a run. Budget ~10 min for the full sweep.
- **One entry point:** `~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh` (capture → compare
  `--all --archive`). It hardcodes the absolute `uv` path.
- **Archive mirror:** every snapshot and comparison is copied to
  `~/DEV/CFB_Forecast_Archive/<season>/`. Read-only copy; truth stays in
  `CFB_Victory_Model/data/`. Registered in `backup-manifest.json` as `personal`/ssd —
  see [[backup-sync-system]] for why a new `~/DEV` folder must be added there.
- The ritual guard still keys off the newest `*_baylor.csv`, which the Big 12 sweep always
  writes, so detection is unaffected.

## A gap can mean the other machine captured it

Confirmed 2026-09-09. The Mac's `data/weekly_forecast_log.csv` looked like it had
missed 2026-08-26 and 2026-08-31 — it jumped 07-31 → 09-02. Neither week was
missed. **Both were captured on the Windows box**, which runs the same wrapper
against the same repo. The two machines had diverged, each holding captures the
other lacked.

Before declaring a missed week, check the other machine's copy of the log.
Merging is safe: the natural key is `(captured_at, season, team, week, game_id)`,
and a union on that key had **zero conflicts** across 216 Mac + 348 Windows rows
→ 540. Same key never carried different values. See [[github-consolidation]].

## An old newest-snapshot file is not proof of a missed week

Checked 2026-09-02: the newest snapshot was `2026-07-31_baylor.csv`, and both the skill and
COMMANDS.md asserted the 08-24 and 08-31 weeks were "gone for good". They were not — Baylor's
opener was 2026-09-05, so no game had been played and nothing had been overwritten. **A week
is lost only if a game was actually played inside the gap.** Verify before declaring a loss:

```
curl -s "https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/football/college-football/teams/239/schedule?season=2026"
```

(239 = Baylor; read each event's `status.type.name`.) Both docs were corrected.

## Cadence

- ~~**Wednesdays**, season window **2026-08-26 → 2027-01-20**~~ — superseded
  2026-08-15. Current cadence is **Monday-anchored**, season window
  **2026-08-24 → 2027-01-23**. See "Cadence" below, which is authoritative.

## The constraint that makes the cadence non-negotiable

**There is no backfill.** A pre-game forecast is only capturable before the game is played;
a missed week is permanently missing from the series, not a chore that rolls
forward. This is why the reminder escalates rather than silently re-queuing.

## Mac-side guard (built 2026-08-15)

`ritual-check.ps1` now carries a fourth ritual, `forecast-capture`, so the cadence is
enforced on this machine rather than depending on memory. It detects captures from the
artifact itself — newest `*_baylor.csv` in `~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/data/weekly_snapshots/`
— matching the script's existing "the artifact is the record, not a state file" rule.

**The real deadline is Saturday's kickoffs, not a maintenance window.** The report
overwrites its Chance of Victory column with the realised result once a game is *played* —
that is what destroyed 2019–2025. Nothing scheduled updates midweek.

Cadence (Monday-anchored, per Eric 2026-08-15 — he wanted the warning early in the week):
**Mon DUE → Tue–Sat OVERDUE → Sun silent** (games played, week gone). Season bounds are the
Monday of the opening week (2026-08-24) and the Saturday of the closing week (2027-01-23),
widened from the documented 08-26 → 01-20 so neither end truncates a live capture window.

A third status, **RECHECK**, exists because an early capture is not proof of a good one: the
source may not have refreshed the coming weekend's numbers on Monday, so a Monday snapshot
can hold last week's figures. Treating "captured this week" as done would let a stale
snapshot pass for a good week — the exact risk that makes capturing early otherwise unsafe.
So a capture taken *earlier* in the week keeps surfacing through Wednesday. Capturing today
always satisfies today; RECHECK means *verify*, not *you missed it*.

Three counterintuitive silences (off-season, Sunday, post-Wednesday-once-captured) plus the
RECHECK window are pinned by `tests/keystone-ritual-forecast-capture.ps1`. Both a
days-since-last-capture and a naive "captured this week → OK" implementation fail them. The
script gained `-Today` and `-CfbSnapshotDir` seams to make this testable.

**`-Notify` was mute on this Mac from the migration until 2026-08-15** — it shelled out to
`msg.exe` (Windows-only), so every scheduled run hit the catch and logged "desktop prompt
unavailable" where nobody reads it. Now `osascript`, dialog with a banner fallback. This
affected *all* rituals, which is consistent with interview-me sitting 12 days overdue and
weekly-review 15. If ritual nags ever go quiet again, test `-Notify` directly before
assuming the rituals are simply current.

Schedule: `com.keystone.rituals` fires Mon–Fri 17:00 plus Fri 15:30, so Monday's DUE and the
Tue–Fri escalation all land. **Saturday and Sunday have no trigger** — Saturday's OVERDUE is
therefore only visible if the script is run by hand. Acceptable because Fri 15:30 and 17:00
are the last useful warnings anyway, but it does mean the Saturday branch is effectively a
manual-run safety net, not a live alarm.

A Windows-side scheduled task `CFB-ForecastCaptureReminder` was left enabled when the
Windows box was retired 2026-08-14 — it operates under that machine's own `~/Desktop/DEV`
and touches none of the Mac repos, so it is harmless but is *not* the authoritative
reminder. See [[backup-sync-system]].

Related model/data work lives in [[cfb-analytics-lab]] (a separate project —
`~/DEV/CFB_Analytics_Lab` vs the Victory Model's own tree).

1	---
2	name: keystoneos-verification-habits
3	description: "Where KeystoneOS state claims are authoritative vs misleading, and which readings have already produced wrong conclusions"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: ea41d487-7812-4180-a6a8-f76a99753f83
8	  modified: 2026-09-12T13:34:11.490Z
9	---
10	
11	This system is well-instrumented, which makes its few misleading surfaces
12	dangerous — they look authoritative. Check these before drawing conclusions.
13	
14	**"Did a job run today?"** Only `KeystoneOS Morning` runs through `run-job.ps1`;
15	AgySync, DailyBackup, MsysKeepAlive, Reconcile, Rituals and StackDoctor invoke
16	their scripts directly and write **no ledger row**. So `outputs/run-ledger.json`
17	under-reports. Correctness is fine — `Test-JobCompleteOn` checks the ledger *or*
18	the job's `successProbe`. Ask `.\scripts\keystone-reconcile.ps1 -DryRun -Json`,
19	never the ledger alone and never `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo`.
20	
21	**memsearch timeout streaks are not failures.** The SessionEnd hook is
22	deliberately best-effort (`daily-backup.ps1:122-125`), wired at `timeout: 50` in
23	`~/.claude/settings.json`; the uncapped nightly absorbs backlog and resets the
24	counter. That nightly moved 00:30 → **09:00 on 2026-08-29**, so a streak now
25	clears in the morning, not overnight. A streak of 16 on 2026-07-28 was
26	read as a broken indexer and produced a whole plan step to "fix" it — the nightly
27	cleared it the same night, exactly as designed. Alarm threshold is 6.
28	
29	**A scheduler's exit code is not the job's outcome.** It reports the last
30	*scheduled* run, so a green log and a red status routinely coexist: a manual or
31	out-of-band run never clears it, and a sleep/wake kill mid-run sets it while the
32	day's work still completed on a later retry. Read the job's own log for a
33	same-day clean end before treating a red status as rot. Two recorded instances:
34	Windows `KeystoneOS-DailyBackup` exit 3221225786 on 2026-08-01 (four killed
35	starts 08:27-11:32, clean end 16:36), and `launchctl list` on 2026-08-31 still
36	showing the failed 09:00 `com.keystone.dailybackup` after the corrected re-run
37	completed with 0 errors. Both cleared themselves at the next scheduled run; a
38	forced re-run would have been cosmetic. (Generalised from the retired
39	Windows-only `backup-task-sleepkill-signature` memory, archived 2026-09-01.)
40	
41	**The test suite is main-checkout-only.** `Get-KeystoneDevRoot` resolves the DEV
42	root as `<repoRoot>\..`, which from a worktree yields
43	`KeystoneOS\.claude\worktrees\`. `tests\keystone-reconcile.ps1` therefore always
44	throws in a worktree. Baseline on main is 23 pass / 1 fail
45	(`skill-verification-contracts.ps1`, unrelated). Always baseline against main
46	before blaming a change.
47	
48	**Three claims failed verification in one session (2026-07-28/29):** that the
49	registry pointed at a stale clone, that the reconciler was wasting hours on
50	redundant backups, and that the indexer was chronically broken. All three were
51	plausible from a point-in-time reading and all three were wrong. State a claim
52	about this system only after re-running the check that produces it.
53	
54	**`canonicalPath` in `data/projects.json` must be a real filesystem path — never a URL.**
55	Learned the hard way 2026-08-15: retiring a project, I set it to the GitHub URL so the field
56	would not point at a deleted directory. That took down the entire 06:00 morning cadence at
57	the dashboard step. `Join-Path`, `Get-Item`, `Resolve-Path`, `Get-ChildItem` and
58	`Convert-Path` all throw *"Cannot find drive. A drive with the name 'https' does not exist"*
59	on a URL. **`Test-Path` is the trap: it returns `False` on a URL instead of throwing**, which
60	is exactly why the `if (-not (Test-Path $Path))` guards in `Get-PathSummary` and
61	`Get-GitSummary` sail past it and the failure lands somewhere further downstream.

63	A path that simply *does not exist* is handled cleanly by those guards, so the correct value
64	for a retired project is its old directory; put the repo URL in a separate field
65	(`restoreFrom`) that nothing treats as a path.

68	The 2026-09-09 GitHub consolidation merge left a **duplicate** `reMarkale_extract` entry in
69	`data/projects.json` whose `canonicalPath` was `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\...`. On macOS
70	that throws *"Cannot find drive. A drive with the name 'C' does not exist"* — identical
71	mechanism to the URL case, different scheme. It killed morning-cadence on **every run from
72	2026-09-10 through 2026-09-12** (5 runs), and the failure was **invisible in the usual
73	places**: `outputs/jobs/morning-cadence-*.{out,err}.log` were both 0 bytes and

---
name: keystoneos-verification-habits
description: "Where KeystoneOS state claims are authoritative vs misleading, and which readings have already produced wrong conclusions"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ea41d487-7812-4180-a6a8-f76a99753f83
  modified: 2026-09-12T13:34:11.490Z
---

This system is well-instrumented, which makes its few misleading surfaces
dangerous — they look authoritative. Check these before drawing conclusions.

**"Did a job run today?"** Only `KeystoneOS Morning` runs through `run-job.ps1`;
AgySync, DailyBackup, MsysKeepAlive, Reconcile, Rituals and StackDoctor invoke
their scripts directly and write **no ledger row**. So `outputs/run-ledger.json`
under-reports. Correctness is fine — `Test-JobCompleteOn` checks the ledger *or*
the job's `successProbe`. Ask `.\scripts\keystone-reconcile.ps1 -DryRun -Json`,
never the ledger alone and never `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo`.

**memsearch timeout streaks are not failures.** The SessionEnd hook is
deliberately best-effort (`daily-backup.ps1:122-125`), wired at `timeout: 50` in
`~/.claude/settings.json`; the uncapped nightly absorbs backlog and resets the
counter. That nightly moved 00:30 → **09:00 on 2026-08-29**, so a streak now
clears in the morning, not overnight. A streak of 16 on 2026-07-28 was
read as a broken indexer and produced a whole plan step to "fix" it — the nightly
cleared it the same night, exactly as designed. Alarm threshold is 6.

**A scheduler's exit code is not the job's outcome.** It reports the last
*scheduled* run, so a green log and a red status routinely coexist: a manual or
out-of-band run never clears it, and a sleep/wake kill mid-run sets it while the
day's work still completed on a later retry. Read the job's own log for a
same-day clean end before treating a red status as rot. Two recorded instances:
Windows `KeystoneOS-DailyBackup` exit 3221225786 on 2026-08-01 (four killed
starts 08:27-11:32, clean end 16:36), and `launchctl list` on 2026-08-31 still
showing the failed 09:00 `com.keystone.dailybackup` after the corrected re-run
completed with 0 errors. Both cleared themselves at the next scheduled run; a
forced re-run would have been cosmetic. (Generalised from the retired
Windows-only `backup-task-sleepkill-signature` memory, archived 2026-09-01.)

**The test suite is main-checkout-only.** `Get-KeystoneDevRoot` resolves the DEV
root as `<repoRoot>\..`, which from a worktree yields
`KeystoneOS\.claude\worktrees\`. `tests\keystone-reconcile.ps1` therefore always
throws in a worktree. Baseline on main is 23 pass / 1 fail
(`skill-verification-contracts.ps1`, unrelated). Always baseline against main
before blaming a change.

**Three claims failed verification in one session (2026-07-28/29):** that the
registry pointed at a stale clone, that the reconciler was wasting hours on
redundant backups, and that the indexer was chronically broken. All three were
plausible from a point-in-time reading and all three were wrong. State a claim
about this system only after re-running the check that produces it.

**`canonicalPath` in `data/projects.json` must be a real filesystem path — never a URL.**
Learned the hard way 2026-08-15: retiring a project, I set it to the GitHub URL so the field
would not point at a deleted directory. That took down the entire 06:00 morning cadence at
the dashboard step. `Join-Path`, `Get-Item`, `Resolve-Path`, `Get-ChildItem` and
`Convert-Path` all throw *"Cannot find drive. A drive with the name 'https' does not exist"*
on a URL. **`Test-Path` is the trap: it returns `False` on a URL instead of throwing**, which
is exactly why the `if (-not (Test-Path $Path))` guards in `Get-PathSummary` and
`Get-GitSummary` sail past it and the failure lands somewhere further downstream.

A path that simply *does not exist* is handled cleanly by those guards, so the correct value
for a retired project is its old directory; put the repo URL in a separate field
(`restoreFrom`) that nothing treats as a path.

**Recurrence 2026-09-12 — same class, cross-machine variant: a Windows drive letter.**
The 2026-09-09 GitHub consolidation merge left a **duplicate** `reMarkale_extract` entry in
`data/projects.json` whose `canonicalPath` was `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\...`. On macOS
that throws *"Cannot find drive. A drive with the name 'C' does not exist"* — identical
mechanism to the URL case, different scheme. It killed morning-cadence on **every run from
2026-09-10 through 2026-09-12** (5 runs), and the failure was **invisible in the usual
places**: `outputs/jobs/morning-cadence-*.{out,err}.log` were both 0 bytes and
`morning-cadence.err` was empty. The only record was `outputs/morning/cadence.log` —
grep it for `cadence FAILED` first, not the job logs. Fixed by deleting the duplicate
(the Mac entry was intact); BOM preserved on the write, see [[settings-json-bom-trap]].

**The asymmetry is the durable lesson: this fault is one-way.** Windows tolerates a
`/Users/...` path (`Test-Path` just returns `False`); macOS *throws* on `C:\` under
`$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"`. So any shared JSON that both machines write will break
the Mac and never the Windows box — and it will recur every time Windows registers a new
project. Expect it after any cross-machine merge; grep shared `data/*.json` for
`eric_rash` or `C:\\` as part of post-merge cleanup. See [[github-consolidation]].

**How to apply:** after editing any `data/*.json` that KeystoneOS scripts consume, run the
consumers before trusting the edit — `scripts/keystone.ps1 dashboard`, `cockpit`, `snapshot`
are quick and cover most path handling. A JSON-validity check proves nothing here; the file
parsed fine and still broke the cadence. See [[morning-briefing-retired]].

1	# STATUS
2	
3	Read this first. Update it before ending every session.
4	
5	Last updated 2026-10-03 (Windows). Evidence for every claim below is in
6	`docs/audits/2026-09-12-gate-a-approval.md`.
7	
8	## Current state
9	- **2026-09-24 (Windows): Windows is the daytime machine, the Mac the evening one.** Two changes follow. First, the ritual nudges move to Windows: `ritual-check.ps1` has a `msg.exe` branch again, and its path defaults now follow the OS, because Mac-only paths made every ritual read "never run" on Windows. Enable `KeystoneOS-Rituals` on Windows and boot out `com.keystone.rituals` on the Mac. Second, `daily-backup` in `data/jobs.json` moves to 21:00 (makeup window 21:00-23:59), so the 07:00 reconcile no longer re-runs it. The CRASHBOX SSD layer only captures if the drive is attached at 21:00.
10	  **Mac half done 2026-09-24 (evening):** `com.keystone.rituals` booted out and `launchctl disable`d (stays off after reboot); `com.keystone.dailybackup` plist Hour 9 → 21 and reloaded (`launchctl print` shows Hour 21). Old plist kept as `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.dailybackup.plist.bak-2026-09-24`.
11	  **2026-10-03 (Windows): Eric's call, keep `KeystoneOS-Rituals` OFF.** Checked: the task is Disabled (last run 2026-08-12). With the Mac job also off, no machine runs the ritual nudges. That is intended. To turn them back on later: `Enable-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'KeystoneOS-Rituals'`.

# Ritual guard.
#
# The 2026-07-24 audits found one pattern in all three systems: everything with
# a cron stayed alive, everything manual froze. interview-me and weekly-review
# both died on 2026-06-05 and nothing noticed for 49 days, because a missing
# ritual leaves no error — it leaves an absence, and absences are invisible.
#
# A cron cannot conduct an interview. What it CAN do is notice the gap and put
# it somewhere unavoidable. That is all this does.
#
# Usage:
#   .\scripts\ritual-check.ps1            # report (runs in the morning cadence)
#   .\scripts\ritual-check.ps1 -Notify    # also raise a desktop prompt if due
#   .\scripts\ritual-check.ps1 -Json      # machine-readable, for the dashboard

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [switch]$Notify,
    [switch]$Json,
    # Overridable so tests can point at a fixture vault. $Root already follows
    # $PSScriptRoot, so copying this script into a temp root redirects the
    # decisions-log lookup for free; only the vault needed a seam.
    # Defaults follow the machine: Windows owns the scheduled nudges since 2026-09-24,
    # and Mac-only paths there made every ritual read "never run".
    [string]$Vault = $(if ($IsWindows) { Join-Path $HOME "Desktop\SecondBrain" } else { "/Users/kristinarash/SecondBrain" }),
    # Same seam rationale as $Vault: the CFB snapshots live outside both $Root and
    # $Vault, so tests need their own pointer at a fixture directory.
    [string]$CfbSnapshotDir = $(if ($IsWindows) { Join-Path $HOME "Desktop\DEV\CFB_Victory_Model\data\weekly_snapshots" } else { "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/data/weekly_snapshots" }),
    # forecast-capture's status depends on the day of the week and on a season
    # window, so it cannot be tested without pinning "now". Defaults to the real
    # clock; only tests pass this.
    [datetime]$Today = (Get-Date),
    # The slate rules live in project-triage (slate.py, tested there). Absolute
    # interpreter path because launchd runs with a bare PATH.
    [string]$Python = $(if ($IsWindows) { (Get-Command python -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Source } else { "/opt/homebrew/bin/python3" }),
    [string]$PortfolioScript = $(if ($IsWindows) { Join-Path $HOME "Desktop\DEV\project-triage\portfolio.py" } else { "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py" }),
    # Empty = the live registry next to portfolio.py. Tests pass a fixture.
    [string]$SlateRegistry = ""
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$Root  = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$today = $Today

# Read the ritual's own output as the record of when it last ran. Deliberately
# not a separate state file: a state file can drift from reality, the artifact
# cannot. If the note exists, the ritual ran.
function Get-LastRun {
    param([string]$Path, [string]$Filter)
    $f = Get-ChildItem $Path -File -Filter $Filter -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
         Sort-Object Name -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
    if (-not $f) { return $null }
    # Prefer the date in the filename over mtime — cloud sync and bulk git ops
    # touch mtimes wholesale and would silently reset the clock.
    if ($f.Name -match '^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})') {
        return [pscustomobject]@{ Date = Get-Date "$($Matches[1])-$($Matches[2])-$($Matches[3])"; File = $f.Name }
    }
    return [pscustomobject]@{ Date = $f.LastWriteTime.Date; File = $f.Name }
}

152	# Window is Monday-anchored, not Wednesday-anchored: the first warning should land
153	# early in the week, with days of runway before Saturday, rather than midweek.
154	$SeasonStart = [datetime]'2026-08-24'   # Monday of the opening week (season opens Wed 08-26)
155	$SeasonEnd   = [datetime]'2027-01-23'   # Saturday of the closing week (window ends Wed 01-20),
156	                                        # so the final week stays actionable through kickoff
157	$fc = Get-LastRun -Path $CfbSnapshotDir -Filter "*_baylor.csv"
158	$fcDays = if ($fc) { [int]($today.Date - $fc.Date).TotalDays } else { 9999 }
159	$inSeason = ($today.Date -ge $SeasonStart.Date) -and ($today.Date -le $SeasonEnd.Date)
160	# Monday anchors the week. Sunday looks back to the Monday six days gone - i.e. the
161	# week that Saturday's games just closed out, which is the right week to judge on a
162	# Sunday (and the answer there is always "nothing to do").
163	$dow = [int]$today.DayOfWeek            # Sunday=0, Monday=1 .. Saturday=6
164	$weekMon = $today.Date.AddDays(-((($dow - 1) + 7) % 7))
165	$capturedThisWeek = ($null -ne $fc) -and ($fc.Date -ge $weekMon)
166	$capturedToday    = ($null -ne $fc) -and ($fc.Date -eq $today.Date)
167	# An early capture is not proof of a good capture. cfbvictorymodel.com may not have
168	# refreshed the coming weekend's numbers yet on Monday, so a Monday snapshot can hold
169	# last week's figures. Going quiet on it would let a stale capture pass for a done
170	# week - so keep surfacing a re-check until Wednesday, by which point the source has
171	# certainly refreshed. Softer than DUE: it means "verify", not "you missed it".
172	$inRecheckWindow = $capturedThisWeek -and (-not $capturedToday) -and ($dow -ge 1) -and ($dow -le 3)
173	$rituals += [pscustomobject]@{
174	    Name    = "forecast-capture"
175	    Command = "/forecast-capture"
176	    Last    = if ($fc) { $fc.Date.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd') } else { "never" }
177	    Days    = $fcDays
178	    Status  = if (-not $inSeason)        { "OK" }
179	              elseif ($inRecheckWindow)  { "RECHECK" }  # captured early - confirm it is not stale
180	              elseif ($capturedThisWeek) { "OK" }
181	              elseif ($dow -eq 1)        { "DUE" }      # Monday - the nag day
182	              elseif ($dow -ge 2)        { "OVERDUE" }  # Tue-Sat - kickoff is coming
183	              else                       { "OK" }       # Sunday - games played, week gone
184	    Why     = if (-not $inSeason) {
185	                  "outside the season window ($($SeasonStart.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')) to $($SeasonEnd.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd'))) - nothing to capture"
186	              } elseif ($inRecheckWindow) {
187	                  "captured $($fc.Date.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')), before the source may have refreshed for this weekend - re-run to confirm the numbers are current"
188	              } elseif ($capturedThisWeek) {
189	                  "captured $($fc.Date.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')) for the week of $($weekMon.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd'))"
190	              } else {
191	                  "the Chance of Victory column is overwritten with the result once a game is played - a week missed before Saturday is gone permanently"
192	              }
193	}

1	# Command desk reference
2	
3	Everything you can run yourself. No agent needed unless a line says so.
4	
5	Built 2026-09-02. Every path here was checked and exists.
6	
7	**Two halves:**
8	
9	- **[Part A](#part-a--terminal-only)** — you type it in Terminal. Claude is not running.
10	- **[Part B](#part-b--needs-claude)** — you type it into Claude Code, or fire it headless with `skill-button.sh`.
11	
12	Copy the commands exactly. They use full paths on purpose, so they work from any folder.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## Part A — Terminal only
17	
18	### A1. Scheduled jobs — run one right now
19	
20	These 8 jobs run on their own. Use `launchctl kickstart` to force one immediately.
21	
22	| Job | Normal time | Run it now |
23	|---|---|---|
24	| Morning cadence (the daily report) | Weekdays 06:00 | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.morning` |
25	| Reconcile (catches missed jobs) | Daily 07:00 | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.reconcile` |
26	| Daily backup | Daily 09:00 | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.dailybackup` |
27	| Graph extract (graphify) | Daily 09:30 | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.graphextract` |
28	| Ritual check | Mon–Fri 17:00, Fri 15:30 | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.rituals` |
29	| Stack doctor | Monday 10:30 | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.stackdoctor` |
30	| Memory adjudicate | Sunday 02:30 | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.adjudicate` |
31	| AGY sync | On demand | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.agysync` |
32	| Command Centre server | Always on | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.commandcentre` |
33	
34	**See if a job is loaded and what it returned last time:**
35	
36	```
37	launchctl list | grep keystone
38	```
39	
40	Column 2 is the last exit code. `0` is good. Anything else means that job died quietly.
41	
42	**Read the columns right.** Column 1 is the PID (a `-` means not running now, which is normal
43	for a job that only runs on a schedule). Column 2 is the **last** exit code, not the current state.
44	
45	Checked 2026-09-02: all 8 scheduled jobs read `0`. Command Centre reads `-15` in column 2 but has
46	a live PID and `localhost:7373` answers `200` — so `-15` is an old exit from before its last
47	restart, not a fault. For a long-running server, trust the PID and the port, not column 2:
48	
49	```
50	curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:7373
51	```
52	
53	**Trap:** `KeystoneOS/data/jobs.json` still says the backup runs at 00:30. That is stale.
54	launchd is the truth, and launchd says 09:00. Do not trust jobs.json for times.
55	
56	---
57	
58	### A2. Daily report — run by hand
59	
60	The same morning report, without launchd.
61	
62	```
63	/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File /Users/kristinarash/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/run-job.ps1 -Job morning-cadence -Trigger manual
64	```
65	
66	Output lands in `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/KeystoneOS/outputs/morning/cadence.log`.
67	
68	---
69	
70	### A3. KeystoneOS — the `keystone` verbs
71	
72	One script, 29 verbs. The verb goes first, with no dash.
73	
74	```
75	/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File /Users/kristinarash/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/keystone.ps1 <verb>
76	```
77	
78	**Read-only. Safe any time:**
79	
80	| Verb | What you get |
81	|---|---|
82	| `status` | Every project: status, branch, uncommitted changes |
83	| `today` | Today's picture |
84	| `morning` | Morning view (this is the default if you give no verb) |
85	| `projects` | Project list |
86	| `health` | System health |
87	| `freshness` | What has gone stale. Age budget is 30 days |
88	| `paths` | Where everything lives |
89	| `inventory` | Full inventory |
90	| `intake` | New things waiting to be sorted |
91	| `graphify` | Knowledge graph state |
92	| `where <key>` | Where one project lives |
93	
94	**These write files or send things. Read the verb before you run it:**
95	`dashboard`, `cockpit`, `start`, `brief`, `plan`, `context`, `closeout`, `control-loop`,
96	`promote`, `heal`, `graphsync`, `okr-link`, `agy-sync`, `meeting-sync`, `snapshot`, `open`,
97	`resume`, `memory`.
98	
99	`dashboard` and `cockpit` sound like views but they build and write files. Checked, 2026-09-02.
100	`freshness -Sweep` deletes merged worktrees. Plain `freshness` only reads.
101	
102	Add `-DryRun` to see what a write verb would do without doing it.
103	
104	**Weekly audit companion:**
105	
106	```
107	/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File /Users/kristinarash/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/ritual-check.ps1
108	```
109	
110	Add `-Notify` to get the macOS notification too. The full weekly audit steps are written up in
111	`/Users/kristinarash/DEV/KeystoneOS/workflows/weekly-audit.md`.
112	
113	---
114	
115	### A4. Backups
116	
117	**Easiest way: type `/backup` in Claude Code.** It runs the script below, reads
118	`backup-state.json` for the verdict, tells you what was skipped, and clears the stale
119	hook error. Use it whenever you remember — the 09:00 job only fires if the Mac is awake.
120	
121	**Run the backup by hand:**
122	
123	```
124	/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File /Users/kristinarash/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1
125	```
126	
127	**Verify it worked (do this, not a guess):**
128	
129	```
130	/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File /Users/kristinarash/.claude/scripts/verify-backup.ps1
131	/Users/kristinarash/.claude/scripts/verify-drive-backup.sh
132	```
133	
134	**Trap:** the backup is default-deny. Every new `~/DEV/<folder>` is skipped until you add it to
135	`/Users/kristinarash/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json`. A new folder means a silent gap.
136	Verify by receipt, never by assuming.
137	
138	---
139	
140	### A5. Memory and search
141	
142	**Memory compiler — daily logs become knowledge articles.**
143	Run this when the startup hook says logs are backlogged:
144	
145	```
146	/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv run --directory /Users/kristinarash/.claude/claude-memory-compiler python scripts/compile.py
147	```
148	
149	| Flag | What it does |
150	|---|---|
151	| `--dry-run` | Show what would compile. Change nothing |
152	| `--all` | Force recompile of every log |
153	| `--file <path>` | Compile one specific daily log |
154	| `--auto` | Unattended. Applies the batch cap |
155	| `--include-quarantined` | Retry logs that failed repeatedly |
156	
157	**Always start with `--dry-run`.** It tells you if there is anything to do at all.
158	Checked 2026-09-02: `Nothing to compile - all daily logs are up to date`. Backlog is clear.
159	
160	**Diagnostic that beats guessing:** count leftover flush files.
161	
162	```
163	ls /Users/kristinarash/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/scripts/session-flush-*.md
164	```
165	
166	`flush.py` deletes its context file on success, so **every leftover file is a flush that died**.
167	"No matches found" is the healthy answer. It is currently 0.
168	
169	**Other compiler scripts** (same `uv run --directory ... python scripts/<name>` shape):
170	`health.py`, `memlint.py`, `adjudicate.py`, `flush.py`, `lint.py`, `query.py`.
171	
172	**memsearch — search all your memory:**
173	
174	```
175	memsearch search "your question here" --top-k 5
176	memsearch stats
177	memsearch config list
178	```
179	
180	**Re-index your memory by hand.** Do not type paths — run the indexer, which reads the real list:
181	
182	```
183	/opt/homebrew/bin/node /Users/kristinarash/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js --worker
184	```
185	
186	**It prints nothing.** That is correct, not a hang. A no-op run takes about 30 seconds; a run
187	with a day of new content can take several minutes. Everything goes to
188	`/Users/kristinarash/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.memsearch-index.log`.
189	Tested 2026-09-02: exit code 0, `Indexed 4 chunks.`
190	
191	**Where the index paths actually live:** `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json`
192	(11 paths). That file is the single source of truth. `memsearch config list` shows `paths = []`,
193	but that is the unused `memsearch watch` setting — **not** the index list. Do not confuse them.
194	
195	**Status, checked 2026-09-02:** healthy.
196	- The 7 timeouts in the startup hook were from **before** the fix landed at 12:33 today. The
197	  SessionEnd hook now detaches a background worker, so it returns in ~42ms and cannot time out.
198	- `.errors.log` is empty (0 bytes) at
199	  `/Users/kristinarash/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`. Empty is correct.
200	- `memsearch stats` reads 11,447 chunks.
201	
202	**Small stale item, not urgent:** two entries in `memory-index-paths.json` are retired Windows
203	slugs (`C--Users-eric-rash...`). They are filtered out by an existence check, so they do no harm.
204	
205	---
206	
207	### A6. Meetings
208	
209	**Sync new Fireflies transcripts into the vault:**
210	
211	```
212	/opt/homebrew/bin/python3 /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/meeting-sync/scripts/sync.py
213	```
214	
215	| Flag | What it does |
216	|---|---|
217	| `--days-back N` | Look back N days |
218	| `--list-only` | Show what would sync. Write nothing |
219	| `--no-sync` | Skip the sync step |

224	/opt/homebrew/bin/python3 /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/meeting-sync/scripts/audit_filenames.py
225	```

227	**Fireflies CLI — meeting reports without the vault:**

241	
242	### A7. CFB — weekly forecast capture
243	
244	Season runs 2026-08-24 to 2027-01-23. **You cannot backfill a missed week.**
245	The nag is Monday-anchored so you get the warning early; **Wednesday is the day to actually
246	run it**, once the model has ingested the weekend. A Monday capture can still hold last
247	week's numbers, which is why the ritual keeps saying RECHECK until Wednesday.
248	
249	Covers **all 16 Big 12 teams**, every week.
250	
251	> **Live status, 2026-09-02.** Big 12 capture run today. Baylor's opener is 09-05, so no
252	> game had been played yet and nothing was lost in the July–August gap. Checked against the
253	> ESPN schedule API, not assumed.
254	
255	**One command. This is the whole job:**
256	
257	```
258	/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh
259	```
260	
261	It captures all 16 teams, prints a rollup plus detail for anything that moved, and copies
262	every snapshot and comparison into `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Forecast_Archive/2026/`.
263	Takes about 10 minutes. A Chrome window opens — that is required.
264	
265	Narrow it by passing arguments straight through:
266	
267	```
268	/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh --team Baylor
269	/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh --teams Baylor TCU "Texas Tech"
270	```
271	
272	Re-read an old comparison without capturing anything:
273	
274	```
275	cd /Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model
276	/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv run python compare_snapshots.py --all
277	/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv run python compare_snapshots.py --team Baylor --list
278	```
279	
280	**Trap 1 — playwright is not installed.** `weekly_capture.py` imports `playwright`, and no Python
281	on this machine has it. Plain `python3 weekly_capture.py` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError`.
282	The `uv run --with playwright` form above fetches it for that one run.
283	
284	Tested end to end 2026-09-02, all green:
285	- `uv run --with playwright` resolves in about 12ms and the script's `--help` runs.
286	- The browser is already cached and matches: Chrome for Testing 151.0.7922.34 (chromium v1234)
287	  in `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium-1234`, marked `INSTALLATION_COMPLETE`.
288	- Nothing to download. If that ever changes, run
289	  `uv run --with playwright python -m playwright install chromium` first.
290	
291	**The `forecast-capture` skill was patched 2026-09-02** to use this same `uv run` form, so
292	`/forecast-capture` works again. Either route is fine now.
293	
294	**Trap 2 — must run headed.** A Chrome window opens. That is correct, not a bug. Headless breaks
295	the Power BI team slicer and Baylor becomes unreachable. Never add `--headless`.
296	
297	**Trap 3 — retries are normal.** `Team attempt 1 failed, retrying...` is expected. It tries 3 times,
298	and any team still failing gets one more full pass at the end of the run. Only worry about names
299	printed in the final `FAILED for:` line.
300	
301	**Trap 4 — no backfill.** The site overwrites the pre-game probability with the real result after
302	kickoff. A missed week is gone forever. But an old snapshot file is **not** proof of a missed week —
303	check whether a game was actually played in the gap before calling it a loss.
304	
305	**Trap 5 — the archive is a copy.** `CFB_Forecast_Archive/` is filled by the wrapper.
306	Truth lives in `CFB_Victory_Model/data/`. Never edit the archive by hand.
307	
308	**Team names must match the report's slicer exactly** — `"Iowa State"` not `"Iowa St."`,
309	`"UCF"` not `"Central Florida"`. The Big 12 list lives in one place: the `BIG12` constant
310	in `weekly_capture.py`. A wrong name fails loudly and prints what the slicer really offers.
311	
312	`CFB_Victory_Model` has no venv and no `pyproject.toml`. The sister repo
313	`/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Analytics_Lab` does have both, but `weekly_capture.py` does not
314	live there — do not go looking for it.
315	
316	**Other files in that folder:** `cfbd_pull.py` (pull fresh data), `evaluate_all_games.py` (score the model).
317

458	## Quick answers
459	
460	**"Run my daily report now."**
461	`launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.morning`
462	
463	**"Did my jobs run?"**

# Command desk reference

Everything you can run yourself. No agent needed unless a line says so.

Built 2026-09-02. Every path here was checked and exists.

**Two halves:**

- **[Part A](#part-a--terminal-only)** — you type it in Terminal. Claude is not running.
- **[Part B](#part-b--needs-claude)** — you type it into Claude Code, or fire it headless with `skill-button.sh`.

Copy the commands exactly. They use full paths on purpose, so they work from any folder.

---

## Part A — Terminal only

### A1. Scheduled jobs — run one right now

These 8 jobs run on their own. Use `launchctl kickstart` to force one immediately.

| Job | Normal time | Run it now |
|---|---|---|
| Morning cadence (the daily report) | Weekdays 06:00 | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.morning` |
| Reconcile (catches missed jobs) | Daily 07:00 | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.reconcile` |
| Daily backup | Daily 09:00 | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.dailybackup` |
| Graph extract (graphify) | Daily 09:30 | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.graphextract` |
| Ritual check | Mon–Fri 17:00, Fri 15:30 | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.rituals` |
| Stack doctor | Monday 10:30 | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.stackdoctor` |
| Memory adjudicate | Sunday 02:30 | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.adjudicate` |
| AGY sync | On demand | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.agysync` |
| Command Centre server | Always on | `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.commandcentre` |

**See if a job is loaded and what it returned last time:**

```
launchctl list | grep keystone
```

Column 2 is the last exit code. `0` is good. Anything else means that job died quietly.

**Read the columns right.** Column 1 is the PID (a `-` means not running now, which is normal
for a job that only runs on a schedule). Column 2 is the **last** exit code, not the current state.

Checked 2026-09-02: all 8 scheduled jobs read `0`. Command Centre reads `-15` in column 2 but has
a live PID and `localhost:7373` answers `200` — so `-15` is an old exit from before its last
restart, not a fault. For a long-running server, trust the PID and the port, not column 2:

```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:7373
```

**Trap:** `KeystoneOS/data/jobs.json` still says the backup runs at 00:30. That is stale.
launchd is the truth, and launchd says 09:00. Do not trust jobs.json for times.

---

### A2. Daily report — run by hand

The same morning report, without launchd.

```
/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File /Users/kristinarash/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/run-job.ps1 -Job morning-cadence -Trigger manual
```

Output lands in `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/KeystoneOS/outputs/morning/cadence.log`.

---

### A3. KeystoneOS — the `keystone` verbs

One script, 29 verbs. The verb goes first, with no dash.

```
/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File /Users/kristinarash/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/keystone.ps1 <verb>
```

**Read-only. Safe any time:**

| Verb | What you get |
|---|---|
| `status` | Every project: status, branch, uncommitted changes |
| `today` | Today's picture |
| `morning` | Morning view (this is the default if you give no verb) |
| `projects` | Project list |
| `health` | System health |
| `freshness` | What has gone stale. Age budget is 30 days |
| `paths` | Where everything lives |
| `inventory` | Full inventory |
| `intake` | New things waiting to be sorted |
| `graphify` | Knowledge graph state |
| `where <key>` | Where one project lives |

**These write files or send things. Read the verb before you run it:**
`dashboard`, `cockpit`, `start`, `brief`, `plan`, `context`, `closeout`, `control-loop`,
`promote`, `heal`, `graphsync`, `okr-link`, `agy-sync`, `meeting-sync`, `snapshot`, `open`,
`resume`, `memory`.

`dashboard` and `cockpit` sound like views but they build and write files. Checked, 2026-09-02.
`freshness -Sweep` deletes merged worktrees. Plain `freshness` only reads.

Add `-DryRun` to see what a write verb would do without doing it.

**Weekly audit companion:**

```
/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File /Users/kristinarash/DEV/KeystoneOS/scripts/ritual-check.ps1
```

Add `-Notify` to get the macOS notification too. The full weekly audit steps are written up in
`/Users/kristinarash/DEV/KeystoneOS/workflows/weekly-audit.md`.

---

### A4. Backups

**Easiest way: type `/backup` in Claude Code.** It runs the script below, reads
`backup-state.json` for the verdict, tells you what was skipped, and clears the stale
hook error. Use it whenever you remember — the 09:00 job only fires if the Mac is awake.

**Run the backup by hand:**

```
/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File /Users/kristinarash/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1
```

**Verify it worked (do this, not a guess):**

```
/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File /Users/kristinarash/.claude/scripts/verify-backup.ps1
/Users/kristinarash/.claude/scripts/verify-drive-backup.sh
```

**Trap:** the backup is default-deny. Every new `~/DEV/<folder>` is skipped until you add it to
`/Users/kristinarash/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json`. A new folder means a silent gap.
Verify by receipt, never by assuming.

---

### A5. Memory and search

**Memory compiler — daily logs become knowledge articles.**
Run this when the startup hook says logs are backlogged:

```
/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv run --directory /Users/kristinarash/.claude/claude-memory-compiler python scripts/compile.py
```

| Flag | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Show what would compile. Change nothing |
| `--all` | Force recompile of every log |
| `--file <path>` | Compile one specific daily log |
| `--auto` | Unattended. Applies the batch cap |
| `--include-quarantined` | Retry logs that failed repeatedly |

**Always start with `--dry-run`.** It tells you if there is anything to do at all.
Checked 2026-09-02: `Nothing to compile - all daily logs are up to date`. Backlog is clear.

**Diagnostic that beats guessing:** count leftover flush files.

```
ls /Users/kristinarash/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/scripts/session-flush-*.md
```

`flush.py` deletes its context file on success, so **every leftover file is a flush that died**.
"No matches found" is the healthy answer. It is currently 0.

**Other compiler scripts** (same `uv run --directory ... python scripts/<name>` shape):
`health.py`, `memlint.py`, `adjudicate.py`, `flush.py`, `lint.py`, `query.py`.

**memsearch — search all your memory:**

```
memsearch search "your question here" --top-k 5
memsearch stats
memsearch config list
```

**Re-index your memory by hand.** Do not type paths — run the indexer, which reads the real list:

```
/opt/homebrew/bin/node /Users/kristinarash/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js --worker
```

**It prints nothing.** That is correct, not a hang. A no-op run takes about 30 seconds; a run
with a day of new content can take several minutes. Everything goes to
`/Users/kristinarash/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.memsearch-index.log`.
Tested 2026-09-02: exit code 0, `Indexed 4 chunks.`

**Where the index paths actually live:** `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json`
(11 paths). That file is the single source of truth. `memsearch config list` shows `paths = []`,
but that is the unused `memsearch watch` setting — **not** the index list. Do not confuse them.

**Status, checked 2026-09-02:** healthy.
- The 7 timeouts in the startup hook were from **before** the fix landed at 12:33 today. The
  SessionEnd hook now detaches a background worker, so it returns in ~42ms and cannot time out.
- `.errors.log` is empty (0 bytes) at
  `/Users/kristinarash/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log`. Empty is correct.
- `memsearch stats` reads 11,447 chunks.

**Small stale item, not urgent:** two entries in `memory-index-paths.json` are retired Windows
slugs (`C--Users-eric-rash...`). They are filtered out by an existence check, so they do no harm.

---

### A6. Meetings

**Sync new Fireflies transcripts into the vault:**

```
/opt/homebrew/bin/python3 /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/meeting-sync/scripts/sync.py
```

| Flag | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--days-back N` | Look back N days |
| `--list-only` | Show what would sync. Write nothing |
| `--no-sync` | Skip the sync step |

**Check for wrong filenames:**

```
/opt/homebrew/bin/python3 /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/meeting-sync/scripts/audit_filenames.py
```

**Fireflies CLI — meeting reports without the vault:**

```
fireflies-pp-cli doctor
fireflies-pp-cli digest
fireflies-pp-cli action-items list
fireflies-pp-cli transcripts search "keyword"
fireflies-pp-cli transcripts status
fireflies-pp-cli topics list
```

Add `--agent` to any of these for JSON instead of text.

---

### A7. CFB — weekly forecast capture

Season runs 2026-08-24 to 2027-01-23. **You cannot backfill a missed week.**
The nag is Monday-anchored so you get the warning early; **Wednesday is the day to actually
run it**, once the model has ingested the weekend. A Monday capture can still hold last
week's numbers, which is why the ritual keeps saying RECHECK until Wednesday.

Covers **all 16 Big 12 teams**, every week.

> **Live status, 2026-09-02.** Big 12 capture run today. Baylor's opener is 09-05, so no
> game had been played yet and nothing was lost in the July–August gap. Checked against the
> ESPN schedule API, not assumed.

**One command. This is the whole job:**

```
/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh
```

It captures all 16 teams, prints a rollup plus detail for anything that moved, and copies
every snapshot and comparison into `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Forecast_Archive/2026/`.
Takes about 10 minutes. A Chrome window opens — that is required.

Narrow it by passing arguments straight through:

```
/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh --team Baylor
/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh --teams Baylor TCU "Texas Tech"
```

Re-read an old comparison without capturing anything:

```
cd /Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model
/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv run python compare_snapshots.py --all
/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv run python compare_snapshots.py --team Baylor --list
```

**Trap 1 — playwright is not installed.** `weekly_capture.py` imports `playwright`, and no Python
on this machine has it. Plain `python3 weekly_capture.py` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError`.
The `uv run --with playwright` form above fetches it for that one run.

Tested end to end 2026-09-02, all green:
- `uv run --with playwright` resolves in about 12ms and the script's `--help` runs.
- The browser is already cached and matches: Chrome for Testing 151.0.7922.34 (chromium v1234)
  in `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium-1234`, marked `INSTALLATION_COMPLETE`.
- Nothing to download. If that ever changes, run
  `uv run --with playwright python -m playwright install chromium` first.

**The `forecast-capture` skill was patched 2026-09-02** to use this same `uv run` form, so
`/forecast-capture` works again. Either route is fine now.

**Trap 2 — must run headed.** A Chrome window opens. That is correct, not a bug. Headless breaks
the Power BI team slicer and Baylor becomes unreachable. Never add `--headless`.

**Trap 3 — retries are normal.** `Team attempt 1 failed, retrying...` is expected. It tries 3 times,
and any team still failing gets one more full pass at the end of the run. Only worry about names
printed in the final `FAILED for:` line.

**Trap 4 — no backfill.** The site overwrites the pre-game probability with the real result after
kickoff. A missed week is gone forever. But an old snapshot file is **not** proof of a missed week —
check whether a game was actually played in the gap before calling it a loss.

**Trap 5 — the archive is a copy.** `CFB_Forecast_Archive/` is filled by the wrapper.
Truth lives in `CFB_Victory_Model/data/`. Never edit the archive by hand.

**Team names must match the report's slicer exactly** — `"Iowa State"` not `"Iowa St."`,
`"UCF"` not `"Central Florida"`. The Big 12 list lives in one place: the `BIG12` constant
in `weekly_capture.py`. A wrong name fails loudly and prints what the slicer really offers.

`CFB_Victory_Model` has no venv and no `pyproject.toml`. The sister repo
`/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Analytics_Lab` does have both, but `weekly_capture.py` does not
live there — do not go looking for it.

**Other files in that folder:** `cfbd_pull.py` (pull fresh data), `evaluate_all_games.py` (score the model).

---

### A8. Graph extract

```
/bin/zsh /Users/kristinarash/DEV/graphify-out/scripts/daily_extract.sh
```

---

### A9. Dashboards to open

**Command Centre — the front door:**

```
open http://localhost:7373
```

The `/os` board lives at `http://localhost:7373/os`. If the page does not load, restart the server:
`launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.keystone.commandcentre`.

**Project board (live, opens a browser):**

```

Reuses the board already running on this machine, else starts one tied to the
terminal. Long form: `python3 ~/DEV/project-triage/board.py --background`
(Windows: `python`, `~/Desktop/DEV`). Flags: `--port N`, `--no-open`.
The static `render.py` dashboard retired 2026-10-03.

**Project status from the terminal:** `portfolio.py set-status <name> active|paused|done`,
`set-receiver <name> "<who>"`, `card-check` (closeout), `sweep` / `sweep-decide` (Friday).

---

### A10. Your other CLIs

All live in `/Users/kristinarash/go/bin/` and are on your PATH.
Every one supports `doctor` (health check) and `--agent` (JSON output).

**Work:**

```

espn-pp-cli injuries

espn-pp-cli leaders
zotero-research-library-pp-cli cache status
zotero-research-library-pp-cli ground "your research question"

```

**Personal (not Baylor work):**

```
flight-goat-pp-cli --help
movie-goat-pp-cli --help
recipe-goat-pp-cli --help
```

**Build a new CLI:** `cli-printing-press --help`

---

## Part B — Needs Claude

### B1. Headless — no chat window

Four skills are wired to run without you typing in a chat. They still use Claude behind the
scenes, but you fire them from Terminal like any other command.

```
/Users/kristinarash/.claude/scripts/skill-button.sh --list
/Users/kristinarash/.claude/scripts/skill-button.sh claude-stack-doctor
/Users/kristinarash/.claude/scripts/skill-button.sh project-triage
/Users/kristinarash/.claude/scripts/skill-button.sh forecast-capture
/Users/kristinarash/.claude/scripts/skill-button.sh closeout
```

**Note on `forecast-capture`:** it is **not** truly headless. The capture must drive a real
Chrome window, so the button needs you logged in at the machine. Do not wire it to launchd.
The skill's run block was fixed 2026-09-02 — see [A7](#a7-cfb--weekly-forecast-capture).

Output goes to `/Users/kristinarash/.claude/scripts/logs/skill-button-<skill>.log`.
Nothing prints to the terminal except errors, so this is safe for launchd or a Shortcut.
Set the model with `SKILL_BUTTON_MODEL` (default `claude-sonnet-5`).

**Stack doctor also has a plain script**, no Claude at all:

```
/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/claude-stack-doctor/scripts/stack-check.ps1
```

---

### B2. Slash commands — type these in Claude Code

**Reports and reviews:**

# Applied Performance — Prioritization Rules

**Why this exists.** "I would start one project, work a little on it, and start a new one because of a random idea or a suggestion. Nothing had a deadline. Done was never defined." — 2026-09-14. Four earlier fixes died because each had to be remembered. These rules are checked by a timer, not by memory.

## The four rules

**1. Active only with a charter.** A job project is active only when it has:
- **Pillar** — data, education, or research — and the JD duty it serves.
- **Receiver** — a named person who asked for it or agreed to receive it. *No name, not active.*
- **Done means** — one sentence: the thing handed over.
- **4 dated steps** — Plan agreed with receiver → First draft to receiver → Final delivered → Receiver confirms it is in use.
- **Finish date** — on or before semester close (2026-12-18).

**2. Four active, no more.** A new project starts only when one is finished or dropped. The one waiting for a slot is "next up." *Fall 2026 exception: cap is 5 so research keeps one project (decided 2026-09-14). Back to 4 in Spring 2027.*

**3. Ideas wait.** New ideas and suggestions go to `/project idea`. Flag an idea only if it has a pillar **and** a receiver. It still waits for a slot.

**4. The timer checks.** `KeystoneOS/scripts/ritual-check.ps1` runs `portfolio.py slate-check` and raises a desktop prompt when:
- more than 4 job projects are active,
- a step date passed and the step is not done,
- a project is past its finish date,
- the Oct 15 checkpoint or Dec 18 semester close was missed,
- an active project has no full charter,
- a slot is open and a project is waiting.

## Where things live

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| The project list, charters, cap | `DEV/project-triage/portfolio.json` (`charter` per project, `meta.slate`) |
| The "why" — objectives and Fall KRs | [[Applied-Performance-OKRs-2026-27]] |
| Check now | `python3 ~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py slate-check` |
| Mark a step done | `python3 ~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py mark-done HPI_Protocol --step 1` |
| Mark a report sent | `python3 ~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py mark-done "report #2"` |
| Project time | One 2-hour calendar block per project per week, placed in open slots: Drive `05_SYSTEMS/ProjectBlocks/fall-2026-project-blocks.ics` |
| Log a block | `/interview-me` asks "which project block, what moved, step done?" (Part 0b) |
| Weekly report | Written every Friday by the timer: `Inbox/weekly-slate/YYYY-MM-DD.md` |
| Pulse to Chris + Kenny | Biweekly status report — Shipped comes from finished steps |

## When a step slips

Do one of three things the same week: **do it**, **re-date it with the receiver** (tell them), or **drop the project** and free the slot. Silent slipping is the only wrong answer.

- `okr-tracker/` — frozen since 2026-06-12, still the June KR set.
- The Thursday unit check-in from the v2 playbook — it needed Blake.

# Handoff — 2026-09-24 — Windows by day, Mac by evening

## What and why

Eric is making Windows the primary daytime machine and the Mac the evening one, so that he
isn't bouncing between them. The session (Windows) started with a question about where the
Drive migration put everything. It then covered cross-machine sync, and finally built what
the day/evening split needs.

## Decisions

- **Windows = day, Mac = evening.** Everything that is text already crosses via GitHub. What was
  still stuck on one machine: the Mac's scheduled jobs and its data, plus Tier A memory.
- **Tier A memory is mirrored.** `dev-sync` runs `~/.claude/skills/dev-sync/mirror_memory.py`,
  which merges the Mac and Windows slug folders (the newer file wins; `MEMORY.md` is merged;
  nothing is deleted). First run: 53 copied, 66 replaced, 16 indexes merged. Pushed as
  dotclaude `e893618`. (claude-skills PR #7)
- **The Mac stays the only writer of GPS, Perch and VALD.** After each pull it writes Parquet
  to `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/athlete-snapshots/{gps,perch,vald}/` with a `manifest.json`.
  There is a stale-writer guard (`--force` overrides). Windows reads the Parquet directly.
  (GPS #3, Perch #1, VALD #4)
- **The Mac daily-backup moves to 21:00**, with a makeup window of 21:00-23:59, so the 07:00
  reconcile doesn't re-run it. The CRASHBOX SSD capture only happens if the drive is attached
  at 21:00. (KeystoneOS #21, claude-skills #8)
- **Ritual nudges move to Windows.** `ritual-check.ps1` has its `msg.exe` branch back, with
  OS-aware paths. The stack doctor now expects `KeystoneOS-Rituals` on Windows and flags
  `com.keystone.rituals` if it is still loaded on the Mac.
- **S2 data lives on Drive:** `04_RESEARCH/03_Active_Studies/S2_Evaluation/data`.
  `build_report.py` resolves `$S2_DATA_DIR`, then Drive, then local `data/`. (S2_Evaluation #1)
  The archived originals were copied in from `08_ARCHIVE/PERSONAL/ThreeStandard/DataConsulting/S2`.
- **GPS `.pbix` is out of scope.** A colleague publishes it and holds the data.

## Mid-flight (not confirmed)

- A message was sent over Remote Control to the Mac session "forecast capture setup". It asks
  that session to (1) set the backup plist to 21:00, and (2) rsync S2 `data/` to Drive. That
  sends `ol_scores.csv` and `team_scores.csv`, which exist only on the Mac. No reply is
  possible, and it may need Eric's approval on the Mac first.

## Next actions

1. **Windows:** run `ritual-check.ps1 -Notify` once, then `Enable-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'KeystoneOS-Rituals'`.
2. **Mac:**
   - `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.rituals`
   - Confirm the backup plist says 21:00 (`launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.dailybackup`).
   - Run `export_snapshot.py --dry-run` and then for real in each of the three pull repos.

4. **Decide:** build a Windows 17:30 auto-push of the context repos only (not DEV projects).
5. **Follow-up:** point Perch's `config.py` / `src/data.py` Windows reads at the Parquet snapshots.

- Windows `git worktree remove` leaves `.git/worktrees/<name>` behind ("Permission denied").
  Clear the read-only attribute, then `Remove-Item -Force`, then `git worktree prune`.
- The auto-mode classifier blocks listing the S2 Drive data folder (athlete-named file), so

# 2026-10-02 — Background job list cleanup (Mac)

## What
Removed 61 completed background sessions from `~/.claude/jobs/` with `claude rm <id>` (Eric approved).
`~/.claude/jobs/` went from 715 MB to 9.3 MB. Repos, memory, transcripts and handoffs were not touched —
`claude rm` deletes only the job record and its `tmp/` scratch folder.

## AIOS sessions removed too
Eric dropped AIOS Task 8 (Pi trial) and approved removing `c59d1788` and `9823c1f0`.
Checked first: Gate C findings fixed on KeystoneOS `main` (`77d9ecc`, `dae7aeb`); monthly
`com.keystone.aiosaudit` ran clean 2026-10-01. Recorded in `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/decisions/log.md`
and `docs/STATUS.md`. `~/.claude/jobs/` is now 64 KB.

## Gotchas
- The auto-mode classifier blocks `claude rm` unless the user approves in chat.
- The AIOS plan's Gate A re-run command points at the removed job scratch; it no longer works.

## Perch-pull fix (same session)
- Cause of the 10/1 `perch-pull` failure: Perch read timeouts (30 s). 20 whole-pull restarts and
  3 failed runs (9/26, 9/27, 10/1) since 9/26. Data never lost; later runs caught up.
- Fix: `_perch_request()` in `~/DEV/PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026/src/perch_ingest.py` retries each
  request (60 s read timeout, 4 tries, 5/15/45 s waits; 4xx not retried). Tests in
  `tests/test_perch.py`, 45/45 pass. Live pull 9/30-10/2 OK (769 rows). Commit `f20a062`, pushed.
- Next: nothing. Check `logs/launchd-perchpull.log` after the 10/3 10:05 run if it ever fails again.
----
# 2026-10-02 — Stack doctor on the Windows laptop

## What and why
Ran `/claude-stack-doctor` on Windows. It found 3 issues: errors-log non-empty,
`MEMORY.md` at 99% of cap, and `~/.claude` 3 commits behind origin.

## Done
- Pulled `~/.claude`. The 3 incoming Mac commits only pruned Mac-slug transcripts,
  plus one regression in `settings.json` (below). Handoff check now reads in sync.
- Removed a hardcoded `/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/dcg` PreToolUse (Bash|PowerShell)
  hook that the Mac had added above the existing guarded `dcg` entry. It errors on
  Windows and double-runs dcg on the Mac. Commit `d59b4dd` in dotclaude, pushed.
- Cleared `transcripts/.errors.log` after archiving it to
  `transcripts/.errors.log.archived-2026-10-02` (4 entries).
- memsearch-sync grpc failure at 21:16 UTC was a Milvus restart; Milvus healthy and
  search working afterwards.

## Decisions
- **Do not re-enable `daily-backup` on Windows.** `daily-backup.ps1` is the Mac port
  (its own header says restore and re-port `daily-backup.ps1.win-orig` first), and running
  it on both machines caused nightly `repo-diverged` in August. Windows is already covered:
  "Backup AI Sessions to Drive" (daily), `Desktop\DEV` as a Drive synced root, and
  `memsearch-drain-weekly` for the reindex.
- **No new pull-only task.** `dev-sync` (also run by `/startup`) already pulls `.claude`,
  skills and global-memory. Run it on sitting down at the laptop.

## Files changed
- `~/.claude/settings.json` (dcg hook removed)
- `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` (emptied)
- `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log.archived-2026-10-02` (new)

## Scheduled job durability

Managed jobs are declared in `data/jobs.json` and started **only** through `.\scripts\run-job.ps1 -Job <id>`, which takes a per-job lock, enforces a timeout, and records the outcome to `outputs/run-ledger.json`. `.\scripts\keystone-reconcile.ps1 [-DryRun] [-Json]` re-runs anything with no success recorded for today; the `KeystoneOS-Reconcile` task fires it at logon (+5m) and hourly.

The rule this encodes: **a scheduled task exiting is not evidence the work happened.** Ask the ledger, or a job's own log via its `successProbe` — never `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo`. On 2026-07-27 the scheduler reported the morning cadence had "successfully completed" with a return code that actually meant the process was killed mid-run. See `decisions/log.md` 2026-07-27 and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-scheduled-job-durability-design.md`.

Re-run `.\scripts\install-reconcile-task.ps1 -Apply` and `.\scripts\harden-scheduled-tasks.ps1 -Apply` after changing task wiring; both are idempotent and dry-run by default.

Front door: when the user says "work on X" / "let's do X" / "resume X", run `.\scripts\keystone.ps1 context <X>` FIRST. It resolves the path (self-healing), shows live git, inlines the brief, points at the project's own CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, and surfaces memory hits + recent decisions — full context in one hop before acting. Paths self-heal on read; `heal` persists a corrected path (auto-commits).

New project into KeystoneOS: `inventory` → `intake` → `promote <path-or-name> -Status "Active"` (writes brief + registry row + projects.json). Map, don't copy — see `decisions/log.md` 2026-06-11.

## Precedence — what wins when two places disagree

Read this before trusting any single file. Two stores disagreeing is the most common way this OS gives a wrong answer.

1. **`AGENTS.md` is the source of truth for routing.** `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md`/`GEMINI.md` defer to it. If they disagree with this table, this table is right and they are stale.
2. **Generated beats hand-written.** `data/*.json` and anything under `outputs/` beat any `.md` prose describing the same registry. `data/projects.json` beats `projects/registry.md`; `data/memory-sources.json` beats any narrative list of sources.
3. **Live check beats recorded state.** Any claim about whether a tool is reachable or authenticated (`connections.md`, tool notes) is a hint, not a fact. Run the check command before acting on it.
4. **Root beats worktree.** `.claude/worktrees/` holds full copies of this repo at older commits. If a search returns two versions of a file, the one at the repo root wins. Never cite a worktree copy as current.
5. **`decisions/log.md` is the decision record.** Newest entry wins on any conflict with older prose elsewhere.

## Operating rules

- KeystoneOS is a map and control plane, not the source repo for every project.
- Do not copy large project files into KeystoneOS. Prefer links and local paths to canonical sources.
- Before multi-step work, find or write a spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/`).
- Before claiming completion, state and run the verification plan (`verification/default-checklist.md`).
- Preserve the existing Claude and Codex memory systems; integrate by reading/querying, not overwriting.
- Use Graphify for comprehension when a repo or corpus is too large to reread directly.

## Harness adapters

`CLAUDE.md` (Claude) and `GEMINI.md` (Gemini) are thin adapters that point here. Keep the three files in sync: shared policy lives in this file only.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

# Audit Workflow

Goal: keep KeystoneOS useful instead of letting it become stale.

Two different questions, two different cadences. Confusing them is how a system stays "well maintained" and still gives wrong answers.

| Question | Tool | Cadence |
|---|---|---|
| Is it **built right**? (structure, coverage) | Four Cs audit, below | Weekly |
| Is it **still true**? (drift, freshness) | `.\scripts\keystone.ps1 freshness` | Every morning, automatic |
| Am I **still doing the rituals**? | `.\scripts\ritual-check.ps1` | Every morning + `KeystoneOS-Rituals` nudge |
| Is it *deeply* still true? (6-check deep audit) | `os-audit` skill | Quarterly |

**Why the ritual check exists.** A skipped ritual produces no error — it produces an absence, and absences are invisible. `interview-me` and `weekly-review` both stopped on 2026-06-05 and nothing noticed for 49 days while every cron-driven surface stayed green. The check reads each ritual's own output as the record of when it last ran (a state file can drift from reality; the artifact cannot).

## Daily — automatic

`freshness` runs inside the morning cadence. It checks hand-written surface age (30-day budget), routing integrity, unmapped top-level folders, root hygiene, stale worktrees, and audit cadence. Output lands in `outputs/morning/cadence.log`. It never fails the cadence — read it, don't rely on it shouting.

Run it manually any time: `.\scripts\keystone.ps1 freshness`, or `freshness -Sweep` to also remove worktrees whose content already landed on main. Locked worktrees are always respected.

## Weekly — Four Cs Audit

Score each out of 25:

- **Context:** current user, priorities, project briefs, decisions. Is `context/priorities.md` still true this week?
- **Connections:** reachable systems. Verify with the check commands in `connections.md` rather than trusting what's written there.
- **Capabilities:** workflows, scripts, skills, harness adapters. Do the three harness adapters still agree?
